newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African stocks ended a volatile day firmly up on Wednesday as buyers returned to a battered market after a heavy sell-off on Tuesday related to the close-out of the December futures contract, dealers said.
Shares started up, boosted by strong gains from Wall Street overnight, but took a knock by noon as futures-related selling kicked in.
However, more positive sentiment began to seep through the market in the afternoon and underlying institutional demand returned, giving stock prices a final leg up in a hectic rush of late trade.
"It has been a volatile day dominated a lot by some of the futures-selling, but there was some good underlying institutional buying," one share dealer said.
The all-share index ended at 6,414.9, up 30.9 points, as industrials rose 66.2 points to close at 7,635.1. Volumes finished well with more than 600 million rand worth of shares being traded.
Most of the buying was in the form of bargain-hunting as dealers sought out stocks that had been oversold on Tuesday.
As a result individual share performances were mixed. Blue-chip Anglos lost 100 cents to 244.00 rand, while SA Breweries put on 150 cents to 110.00 rand.

One of the main beneficiaries of the day was mining house Impala Platinum which ended the day up 16.05 percent, or 650 cents, at 47.00 rand. Dealers said the stock had suffered heavily during the close-out and was now being snapped as oversold. It was also up on the back of a firmer platinum price.
One stock that did not perform well was De Beers which ended the day down 300 cents at 129.50 rand despite news of record rough diamond sales in 1996.

The share took a hammering after the firm said it would stop buying Russian stones under an old marketing agreement after December 31 and gave the Russian authorities until then to sign a new pact, which has been on hold since February.
Dealers said all market eyes would be on the performance of Wall Street overnight for further guidance to South Africa's sensitive markets.
"If Wall Street does well again we could be flat to firmer tomorrow (Thursday)," one dealer said.
The golds sector, which took a serious dive on Tuesday, bounced back slightly and managed to tenaciously hold onto its modest early gains as the global bullion price firmed.
The gold index finished up 11.0 points at 1,488.7.
South African share futures had a healthy day as the market tentatively readjusted after Tuesday's close-out. But little real demand was seen for equities.
The all-share March contract stood at 5,990/6,005 from 5,823, the industrial contract at 7,520/30 from 7,328 and gold contract at 1,043/50 from 1,043.
